sections.h2: How to sell a Lewisville house fast
sections.html:
You can sell a Lewisville house to a cash buyer or list it, and repairs plus your deadline usually settle the question. Located in Denton County in the north Dallas-Fort Worth area, the city has rental and tax rules that influence what investors and owner-occupants will pay.

If the house has been a rental, look at the city's rental inspection and short-term rental rules first. Buyers who plan to keep it as a rental will ask about both.

The city's fiscal 2026 rate is $0.419009 per $100. Because the county and school district add their own levies, your statement from the Denton County tax office shows the total you owe.

The median residential bill is $6,606, split 65 percent to Lewisville ISD, 24 percent to the city and 11 percent to Denton County. In dollars that is $4,294 for the school district, $1,585 for the city and $727 for the county. A penny on the city rate raises about $2.154 million. The school district drives most of what a buyer will pay each year, and the city's share is the smaller piece.

Lewisville runs an inspection program for single-family rentals, with no fee or registration, that began July 1, 2008. Three things trigger an inspection: the owner or a future tenant telling the city, a tenant asking for a water transfer, or a complaint. Minor violations do not block move-in, but life-safety issues do. Apartments, mobile homes and houses outside city limits are not covered.

The Code Enforcement Division runs the program, and its number is 972.219.3470. The inspection list works as a handy checklist for any seller, rented or not.

  • House number visible from the street.
  • Roof, gutters, siding and exterior doors in repair.
  • Windows and screens intact, and fences or pool fences maintained.
  • Electrical service drop at least 10 feet above the ground and the meter secured.
  • Grass, weeds, hedges and trees along the right-of-way trimmed.
  • No inoperable vehicles, no cars parked on grass and no standing water.

Clearing these items before you list avoids a code complaint that could surface mid-sale, and it removes a common buyer objection.

Lewisville issues short-term rental permits yearly and stops at 150 active ones.

Lewisville short-term rental rules
RuleRequirement
Permit termOne year, not transferable
Application fee$400, non-refundable
Active permit cap150
Spacing, single-family or duplex1,000 feet between rentals
Multifamily limit3% of units or 2 units, whichever is greater

A permit stays with the owner and address, so a buyer who wants to host guests must apply fresh, with no promise of approval. Existing permitted rentals are treated as legal non-conforming until the use stops for six months. Hotel occupancy tax is reported monthly.

sections.h2: What a short-term rental buyer will ask
sections.html:
If your house was listed on a booking site, expect questions about the permit. The application closes when permits plus pending applications reach the cap of 150, and it reopens if permits are denied, revoked or expire. Current holders can reapply at least 30 days before expiry even when applications are closed.

  • A bedroom needs at least 70 square feet, and 50 square feet per person when more than one person shares it.
  • A 70 to 99 square foot bedroom counts as one occupant, and 100 to 149 as two.
  • Ads must show the permit number and say the unit cannot host paid events or parties.
  • More than two city code citations in a permit year can lead to revocation.

Because a permit cannot be transferred, the buyer starts in the application queue. The permitting office at permitting@cityoflewisville.com or 972.219.3470 can say whether space is open.

Bills arrive in the fall and are usually due by January 31. The lien attaches on January 1, so the owner on that date is responsible for the year's tax.

  • An over-65 or disabled homeowner can ask the county about a four-payment plan.
  • A value protest is due by May 15 or 30 days after notice, whichever comes later.
  • After the appraisal board, appeals can go to district court or arbitration.

Get a current payoff and tax statement from the Denton County tax office before closing.

sections.h2: If a Lewisville house is in trouble
sections.html:
A lien for unpaid tax can end in a tax sale. A former owner can redeem land sold at a tax sale, paying a stated premium, within two years for a homestead or 180 days for other property. Any excess from a tax foreclosure can be claimed by the former owner for two years.

Should a tenant remain after the sale, the new owner may have to file an eviction case in justice court, where the tenant receives at least four days' notice of the trial. Selling before any of this starts keeps your options open.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants in the house
sections.html:
Many Lewisville houses are rented at some point. If yours is, decide before listing whether the buyer will take the lease or you will deliver the house empty. Tell the tenant early and in writing. A buyer who wants to keep the house as a rental will ask whether it passed the city's single-family rental inspection, and records of past inspections answer that fast.

An investor will often take a leased house as it stands. A buyer who wants to live in it needs possession, which means ending the lease on a schedule that fits the closing date. Put that schedule in the contract so nobody guesses.

sections.h2: Talking to the city before you list
sections.html:
A short call to the Code Enforcement Division can settle questions that would otherwise show up during the buyer's inspection. Ask whether any complaint or violation is open on the address, whether a rental inspection is on record and, for a house used for guests, whether a short-term rental permit is active. Ask the permitting office whether any permit for work on the house is still open.

Keep a note of who answered, and send the buyer or closing office whatever the city confirms.

sections.h2: What to have ready before accepting an offer
sections.html:
• A copy of the deed and any survey.
  • The latest Denton County tax statement and exemption list.
  • Rental inspection or short-term rental permit records, if the house was rented.
  • A payoff letter from your lender.

With those four items in hand, a buyer or the closing office can move from contract to closing without waiting on you. If you are unsure what the city has on file for the address, call Code Enforcement at 972.219.3470 and ask about open violations or permits before you list.

1. Fix or note any exterior items from the inspection checklist.
  2. Get offers from a cash buyer and, if you choose, a listing agent.
  3. Compare what each leaves you after the loan payoff and the year's tax share.
  4. Sign with a notary and let the closing office record the deed.

A cash buyer can skip the lender's appraisal and many repair requests, which is why the process can finish sooner. A listing may bring a higher price but adds showings and a buyer's loan timeline.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Lewisville house if it was a rental?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers may ask whether it passed the city's single-family rental inspection, so have any records ready.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take over my Lewisville short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. A permit cannot be transferred. The new owner applies on their own, under the 150-permit cap and the spacing rules.

faqs.q: What is the Lewisville property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's rate is $0.419009 per $100 for fiscal 2026. Your full bill also includes Denton County and the school district, so check your statement.

faqs.q: When are Denton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: In most cases by January 31, with penalty and interest from February 1. Some owners can use a split or installment plan.

faqs.q: Do I need Lewisville city approval to sell my home?
faqs.a: No city approval is needed just to sell. Contact the city if you have open code violations or permits, since a buyer will want those resolved.
